Independent external review by @ProfHepta, bound to current head 898c0e0166e492b1263d809c3c56bfe600a4838e.

COMMENTED disposition: KEEP DRAFT / NO MERGE. I reviewed the D6 source-gap closure scope and claim ceiling. The current exact-head matrix is still non-terminal: integrated-image/qualification lanes are in progress, even though the source, governance and Rust lanes shown so far succeeded. Preserve merge_ready=false and the explicit limits on protected-main/team CODEOWNERS, signing custody, exact-main promotion, QEMU/Servo/D1/D2I, cross-UID activation and release authority. Complete a terminal exact-head matrix and independent governance review before any ready state; no self-merge or admin/auto bypass. Any push invalidates this review.

External full-gap/governance review by `Franksudoman`, bound to exact current head `08d4921851accb66f924152c2f067c3b396db77d`.

**REQUEST_CHANGES — KEEP DRAFT / `merge_ready=false`.**

The PR body freezes candidate head `2e6f227b…` and tree `ef51a2ac…`, but the live head is `08d49218…`. Ten exact-head workflows succeed, while `d2i-integrated-image` run `33353877221` fails. Consequently the locally described two-preparation equality and historical D1/D2I evidence cannot qualify the current object or downstream #53/#54.

Repair the D2I machine failure and rerun the complete non-empty exact-head collection. Refresh commit/tree/run/receipt identities; independently verify source-epoch-bound ext4 metadata normalization, exact e2fsprogs source/version custody, two-preparation byte equality, fail-closed dynamic command-graph scanning, D1 epoch bounds and the distinction between ephemeral object fetches and remote protected-ref writes. Any source or base change invalidates the matrix.

Repository ruleset readback currently shows none, so protected-main, required-check, team-CODEOWNERS, independent approvals and no-bypass claims remain external. Signing, exact-main promotion, live cross-UID activation and D4–D9 authority remain false. No merge, auto-merge or administrator bypass was performed.

External exact-head review for `da9151daf8b1bdccd8120a770e352757f8fba12d` — changes requested.

Blocking D3 identity-semantic defect: the new static executable mode does not bind the connected peer process to the executable whose digest is placed in its attestation snapshot.

`read_snapshot_with_source` reads PID/UID/GID/start-time/cgroup/unit from the peer's procfs entry, but for `ExecutableSource::Static` it independently reopens and hashes the configured pathname. `attest_with_static_executable_digest` then stores that unrelated fixed-path digest in the peer snapshot. The development daemon supplies `/usr/libexec/hepta-agent` and uses the resulting snapshot digest to construct the TaskFlow principal.

There is no proof that the peer PID is executing that file. Any other process satisfying the expected `hepta-agent` UID/GID and `/system.slice/hepta-agent.service` cgroup/unit checks receives the same trusted-path digest; the pidfd and start-time checks prove process continuity, not executable provenance. The resulting principal therefore overstates a service-mechanism check as an exact executable identity binding.

Use a trusted supervisor/launch record that cryptographically or descriptor-wise binds the exact PID/process instance to the opened executable identity, or model this explicitly as the weaker service-unit mechanism and do not populate/grant an executable-bound principal until actual process-to-image provenance is available. Add a negative test with a different executable process in the same authorized UID/GID/cgroup/unit and require rejection.

The current head's eleven discovered PR workflows are terminal successful, but they do not prove this missing relationship. The PR description is also materially stale: it still freezes head `2e6f227b…` and a D6-only scope, while the live candidate is a 20-commit, 219-file head containing D3 activation work.

Keep Draft and `merge_ready=false`. Refresh the scope and exact identity after repair, then rerun the complete matrix and obtain fresh independent review. Do not self-merge, enable auto-merge, mark ready, or use an administrator bypass.
